rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Carbon gets its own shelf for **three reasons**. **Numbers:** catenation plus isomerism has produced tens of millions of organic compounds — more than all other chemistry combined. **Properties:** organic compounds are covalent molecules — low m.p./b.p., flammable, non-conducting, organic-solvent soluble, isomer-rich, slow-reacting — while inorganic compounds are largely ionic lattices with the opposite profile in…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Silane stops, hexane continues*** — Si–Si bonds are too weak for long chains, so silicon's hydrides end at a few atoms; carbon's strong C–C bond lets chains run to millions of units — the numeric root of the separate study.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The organic/inorganic border is behavioural, not geographical: what separates the shelves is molecular covalency versus ionic lattices — and that single cause drives every row of the comparison table.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Three reasons for separate study: (1) numbers — organic compounds outnumber all others (catenation + isomerism); (2) properties — covalent molecular: low mp/bp, flammable, non-conductors, organic-solvent soluble, isomerism common, slow molecular reactions vs ionic fast reactions; (3) methods — extraction,…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Tens of millions of organic compounds are registered — more than all other chemistry combined — and the count grows by millions per decade.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Carbon Gets Its Own Shelf Organic chemistry is not studied separately by tradition but by necessity. Three facts force the separation: organic compounds are **vastly more numerous**, they behave **differently** (covalent, flammable, low-melting, isomer-rich), and they must be **studied by different methods**.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Reason 1 — sheer numbers - More organic compounds are known than compounds of **all the other elements combined** (tens of millions). - The cause is **carbon's self-linking (catenation)** plus **isomerism**: one molecular formula can hide many compounds, and chains of any length can carry any functional group.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Catenation** | Self-linking of atoms of an element into chains/rings | C–C–C… in alkanes | | **Isomerism** | Same molecular formula, different compounds | C₂H₆O: ethanol, dimethyl ether | | **Molecular compound** | Discrete covalent molecules with weak intermolecular forces | CH₄, C₂H₅OH |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Electrons orbit in fixed paths like planets. ✅ Electrons exist in probability clouds (orbitals).  ·  ❌ Heisenberg uncertainty means we cannot measure position and momentum precisely simultaneously — not that we lack good instruments.  ·  ❌ de Broglie wavelength applies only to light. ✅ All matter has wave nature; detectable mainly for small masses like electrons.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Quantum number l can be any integer. ✅ l ranges from 0 to n−1.  ·  ❌ Magnetic quantum number ml determines energy. ✅ ml determines orbital orientation, not energy (in absence of magnetic field).  ·  ❌ Spin quantum number ms can be ±½ or any value. ✅ ms is always +½ or −½.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Aufbau principle means filling from bottom to top of the diagram. ✅ Fill lowest-energy orbitals first: 1s→2s→2p→3s→3p→4s→3d→4p→...  ·  ❌ Pauli exclusion allows two electrons per orbital with any spin. ✅ Two electrons in same orbital must have opposite spins.  ·  ❌ Hund's rule means pair electrons before spreading. ✅ Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly first with parallel spins.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The mole is just a number like dozen. ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant) — a bridge between atomic and macroscopic scales.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is in amu; molar mass is in g/mol — numerically equal but different units.  ·  ❌ Limiting reagent is the reactant with smallest mass. ✅ Limiting reagent is the one that produces the least product (determined by moles, not mass).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ % yield can exceed 100%. ✅ % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying.  ·  ❌ Molarity and molality are the same. ✅ Molarity = mol/L solution (changes with T); Molality = mol/kg solvent (temperature-independent).  ·  ❌ A strong acid completely ionizes in water. ✅ Strong acids (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄) are ~100% ionized; weak acids partially ionize.
